messages.author: af38901b4ca34000
messages.subject: Time series stacked line plots with different time intereval
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to plot a stacked line plot that has five variables using "facets" command. I have been able to stack the plots; however, since the time step for each variable is not the same, the ones that are at lower resolution have only dots, no lines. Is there a way to stack the plots using same time scale (x-axis); however, still plotting lines or even bars? I have attached the plot for your reference. What I am intending to accomplish is to have lines at the bottom three plots. The time step for upper three plots is month and for lower three is year.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Time series stacked line plots with different time intereval
parts:
I'll try to pinch hit for Ista since he appears to be busy at the moment. His advice about removing NAs in Vars 4-6 is correct, as usual; here's one way to do it. Call this the split-reshape-combine approach :)


library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)

# try() is the name of a common function in R, so rename
Try = read.csv(file="Data.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",")
Try$Date = as.Date(Try$Date, format='%d/%m/%Y')

# Create two sub-data frames: one for the first three variables,
# another for the latter three, both including Date
try0 <- Try[, 1:4]
try1 <- Try[, c(1, 5:7)]

# logical vector to determine if any of Var4-Var6 are nonzero
# in a given row of try1; use this for subsetting below
v <- apply(try1[, -1], 1, function(x) any(!is.na(x)))

trym0 <- melt(try0, id = "Date")     # 738 x 3
trym1 <- melt(try1[v, ], id = "Date")    # 45 x 3

# Note: variable has different levels in trym0 and trym1

# The two data frames have the same variables, so rbind them
trym <- rbind(trym0, trym1)
# redefine the factor 'variable' to get all of the levels from both
trym$variable <- factor(trym$variable)

# Now plot...
qplot(Date, value, data=trym, colour = variable, size = I(1.2)) + geom_line() +
facet_grid(variable ~ ., scales = "free")

Observe that you still get a gap in the line plot of Var4, but that's because it has missing values for three years where Vars 5 and 6 do not. The gap is informative. You see the same thing in Var1, but it's less obvious due to the data density. I reduced the point size to reduce overlap of the points - if you like the original point size, just get rid of the argument in qplot(). (size = 1.3 will give you visually larger points).

Dennis
